tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__getAccessibleAtlassianResources
tools.description: Returns the cloudId(s) available to the current user. Not needed when the user gives a Jira or Confluence link: other tools accept the link's site hostname (e.g. example.atlassian.net) as cloudId.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__getJiraIssue
tools.description: Get a Jira or JSM issue by key or ID. Use for one known issue; use searchJiraIssuesUsingJql to find or list many issues. Reports how many comments an issue has, not the comments themselves — for those use listJiraIssueComments. View "evidence" also returns the issue's links to other issues.

cloudId.description: Atlassian site UUID, hostname, or URL. If unknown, list accessible resources.

issueIdOrKey.description: Issue key (PROJ-123), numeric ID, or a Jira issue URL

fields.description: Custom Jira field IDs to fetch (e.g. ["customfield_10010", "customfield_10020"]). Overrides the view's fetch strategy. For custom fields in normal use, prefer view: "evidence", which fetches and maps them automatically. Use ["*all"] to fetch every field (expensive — prefer view: "full" instead).

includeEditableFields.description: When true, also return compact metadata for fields the authenticated user can edit on this issue, including type, allowed values, and operations. Omit unless preparing an edit: this makes an extra Jira REST call.

fieldsByKeys.description: When true, each entry in `fields` is interpreted as a Jira field key (e.g. "summary", "description") instead of a field id. Matches the Jira REST `fieldsByKeys` query parameter. Ignored when `fields` is omitted (default field list uses ids).

expand.description: Additional Jira expand tokens (comma-separated), e.g. "renderedFields,changelog". Merged with any expand the server adds for custom-field mapping (e.g. "names"); duplicate tokens removed. Note "changelog" here returns only the newest page, sorted newest-first, and it accepts startAt/maxResults then ignores them — so it cannot be paged and reports a longer history as complete. Use listJiraIssueChangelogs to read all of it (oldest-first); do not mix their orderings.

properties.description: Issue entity property keys to return (Jira `properties` query param, repeated per key). Omit unless you rely on app-specific issue properties.

failFast.description: When true, forwards Jira's `failFast` query flag for this GET. Omit for Jira default behavior.

responseContentFormat.description: Format for rich-text bodies — description and environment, plus any comment bodies the view returns. Defaults to markdown. Set html to receive HTML, which is lossless, so you can pass it straight back to editJiraIssue/addOrEditJiraIssueComment with contentFormat: html. Bodies holding anything markdown cannot represent — inline media, panels, expands, layouts, statuses, @mentions, dates, emoji — are returned as HTML automatically, because markdown would drop those nodes or turn them into literal text on write-back. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

actionSource.description: Optional invocation attribution. Jira MCP cards set jira_mcp_card; omit for model/tool-loop calls.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__getPeopleInfo
tools.description:
(Beta) Get people’s profiles and optional immediate reporting relationships. Provide cloudId and exactly one selector: identifier (an array of 1–10 Atlassian account IDs or IdentityUser ARIs), name, or email. Name and email each resolve one person; use name: "me" for yourself. If a name is ambiguous, use the returned candidates to disambiguate with an account ID or exact email; do not guess. The profile is always requested. Set manager: true, directReports: true, or both in one call. Results contain identity and requested reporting facets, each with a status. Use successful results when others fail; partial or unavailable data does not establish that a relationship is absent. Reporting relationships do not establish expertise, ownership, or delivery responsibility.

This tool is in beta and is not generally available. Usage is not billed during beta. Pricing details will be announced when the tool becomes generally available.

cloudId.description: Atlassian site UUID, hostname, or URL. If unknown, list accessible resources.

identifier.description: One or more Atlassian account IDs or IdentityUser ARIs (maximum 10). Cannot be combined with name or email.

name.description: Resolve target user by name, or "me" for the current user. Ambiguous names require disambiguation.

email.description: Resolve target user by exact email, or "me" for the current user.

directReports.description: Request direct reports alongside the profile. Can be combined with manager.

manager.description: Request the immediate manager alongside the profile. Can be combined with directReports.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__listJiraIssueComments
tools.description: Get a paginated list of comments for a Jira issue. Use this instead of getJiraIssue when an issue has many comments — getJiraIssue embeds at most 20 and cannot page them. Page with startAt until isLast is true; total is the full comment count. Each comment reports any visibility restriction on it and, on JSM, whether it is internal (jsdPublic: false) — check both before quoting or summarising a comment. Comments are returned as a flat list: a non-null parentId means the comment is a reply, and parentId identifies its root/parent comment. Group comments by parentId to reconstruct threads. Set reactionDetail when emoji reaction data is needed. For the issue's own fields, use getJiraIssue.

cloudId.description: Atlassian site UUID, hostname, or URL. If unknown, list accessible resources.

issueIdOrKey.description: Issue key (PROJ-123), numeric ID, or a Jira issue URL

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first comment to return (for pagination). Defaults to 0.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of comments to return per page (1-100). Defaults to 100. Read total from the response for the full count. With view: "full" the page is capped at 20, because a larger full-view page can exceed the client's token limit and fail the whole call; the response echoes the effective value.

orderBy.description: Order comments by created date — "created"/"+created" (oldest first) or "-created" (newest first).

expand.description: Comma-separated list of extra data to include on each comment, e.g. "renderedBody" (HTML-rendered body) or "properties".

responseContentFormat.description: Format for comment bodies. Defaults to markdown. Set html to receive HTML, which is lossless, so a body can be passed straight back to addOrEditJiraIssueComment with contentFormat: html. Fetch as html before editing any comment, since markdown drops images, panels and expands and returns statuses/@mentions as literal text. A page holding any such comment is returned as HTML automatically. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

reactionDetail.description: Reaction enrichment level. "none" (default) returns comments only, with no Reactions API call. "summary" adds emoji counts and whether the current user reacted. "users" also names who reacted — ask for it only when attribution is requested, since it costs an extra request per distinct emoji and reports when it could not expand every one.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql
tools.description: Search for Jira issues using JQL, with an optional approximate count. Use view: "evidence" to fetch and map custom fields. Page with nextPageToken until isLast is true. For one known issue, use getJiraIssue. JQL only returns issues; inferring anything else from issue rows is silently incomplete. For the discussion of several issues add "comment" to fields; for their recent status history add "changelog" (when enabled on the site). Add only the one the question needs, since each adds a page of items per row, and do not read them issue by issue afterwards. Scope the JQL to the set the question is about: a stand-up or "current work" is the active sprint (sprint in openSprints()) or one assignee, so backlog and closed-sprint items are not reported as current work; a question about the whole project (what changed, bottlenecks, time in status) is one project-wide search. For one issue's complete history or thread use listJiraIssueChangelogs or listJiraIssueComments. For the time logged on several issues add "worklog" to fields (when enabled on the site); for one issue's complete time log, or a date window, use listJiraIssueWorklogs. Use the purpose-built operation for sprints, boards, board config, releases, accountIds, issue types, projects and statuses. Searches span all projects unless you add a project clause; for cross-team or related-work questions, leave it out or use `project in (A, B)`.

cloudId.description: Atlassian site UUID, hostname, or URL. If unknown, list accessible resources.

jql.description: JQL query string e.g. "project = PROJ AND status = 'In Progress'", or across all projects 'text ~ "PROJ-123" ORDER BY updated DESC'. If the tool returns a repairHint, follow it and retry.

searchResultMode.description: Default "issues". Never count for normal search or if nextPageToken used. If total for same query is known, reuse it. Use "count" only when no trusted count exists and either the user asks or a downstream step needs it. Use "all" only if both count and issues required.

fields.description: Fields per issue (e.g. ["summary", "status", "customfield_10010"]). Omit for view defaults. Explicit fields remain view-filtered. Use evidence for parent, resolution date, descriptions, reporter details and fix-version names; full with minimal fields for data outside both presets, including issue links. Discover site-specific customfield_* IDs; custom field values map to issues[].fields.customFields. Explicit IDs avoid evidence's all-field fetch default.

nextPageToken.description: Pagination token from a previous response to fetch the next page

responseContentFormat.description: Format for rich-text bodies (description, environment, comments) when the view returns them. Defaults to markdown; html is lossless for a later editJiraIssue. Issues holding anything markdown cannot represent (media, panels, expands, statuses, @mentions) are returned as HTML automatically, decided per issue. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

actionSource.description: Optional invocation attribution. Jira MCP cards set jira_mcp_card; omit for model/tool-loop calls.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

fieldsByKeys.description: When true, each entry in `fields` is interpreted as a Jira field key (e.g. "summary", "description") instead of a field id. Matches the Jira REST `fieldsByKeys` query parameter. Ignored when `fields` is omitted (default field list uses ids).

expand.description: Additional Jira expand tokens (comma-separated), e.g. "renderedFields,changelog". Merged with any expand the server adds for custom-field mapping (e.g. "names"); duplicate tokens removed. Note "changelog" here returns only the newest page, sorted newest-first, and it accepts startAt/maxResults then ignores them — so it cannot be paged and reports a longer history as complete. Use listJiraIssueChangelogs to read all of it (oldest-first); do not mix their orderings.

properties.description: Issue entity property keys to return (Jira `properties` query param, repeated per key). Omit unless you rely on app-specific issue properties.

failFast.description: When true, forwards Jira's `failFast` query flag for this GET. Omit for Jira default behavior.

responseContentFormat.description: Format for rich-text bodies — description and environment, plus any comment bodies the view returns. Defaults to markdown. Set html to receive HTML, which is lossless, so you can pass it straight back to editJiraIssue/addOrEditJiraIssueComment with contentFormat: html. Bodies holding anything markdown cannot represent — inline media, panels, expands, layouts, statuses, @mentions, dates, emoji — are returned as HTML automatically, because markdown would drop those nodes or turn them into literal text on write-back. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

actionSource.description: Optional invocation attribution. Jira MCP cards set jira_mcp_card; omit for model/tool-loop calls.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__listJiraIssueComments
entries.description: Get a paginated list of comments for a Jira issue. Use this instead of getJiraIssue when an issue has many comments — getJiraIssue embeds at most 20 and cannot page them. Page with startAt until isLast is true; total is the full comment count. Each comment reports any visibility restriction on it and, on JSM, whether it is internal (jsdPublic: false) — check both before quoting or summarising a comment. Comments are returned as a flat list: a non-null parentId means the comment is a reply, and parentId identifies its root/parent comment. Group comments by parentId to reconstruct threads. Set reactionDetail when emoji reaction data is needed. For the issue's own fields, use getJiraIssue.

cloudId.description: Atlassian site UUID, hostname, or URL. If unknown, list accessible resources.

issueIdOrKey.description: Issue key (PROJ-123), numeric ID, or a Jira issue URL

startAt.description: Zero-based index of the first comment to return (for pagination). Defaults to 0.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of comments to return per page (1-100). Defaults to 100. Read total from the response for the full count. With view: "full" the page is capped at 20, because a larger full-view page can exceed the client's token limit and fail the whole call; the response echoes the effective value.

orderBy.description: Order comments by created date — "created"/"+created" (oldest first) or "-created" (newest first).

expand.description: Comma-separated list of extra data to include on each comment, e.g. "renderedBody" (HTML-rendered body) or "properties".

responseContentFormat.description: Format for comment bodies. Defaults to markdown. Set html to receive HTML, which is lossless, so a body can be passed straight back to addOrEditJiraIssueComment with contentFormat: html. Fetch as html before editing any comment, since markdown drops images, panels and expands and returns statuses/@mentions as literal text. A page holding any such comment is returned as HTML automatically. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

reactionDetail.description: Reaction enrichment level. "none" (default) returns comments only, with no Reactions API call. "summary" adds emoji counts and whether the current user reacted. "users" also names who reacted — ask for it only when attribution is requested, since it costs an extra request per distinct emoji and reports when it could not expand every one.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

fields.description:
Finding G17 asks for DCU, tempr and period overrides for the ReLIVE data. The overrides in `src/core/override_scheme.py` hold LUCIA values only: site date periods (RI-Site1, BC-Site1, AN-Site1), DCU numbers 1107–1117, breath-number fixes and PCB temperature limits. `preprocessing.apply_overrides` switches all of them on or off together. Checked on master b0e17b0, 2026-11-27.

Needed from <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Avichai Toubi</custom> and <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-1">@Gilad Feinberg</custom>:

1. Which DCU numbers to invalidate or remove for ReLIVE.
2. Which date periods, per site.
3. The temperature limits for the ReLIVE PCBs.
4. Where these values come from.

Then: add the ReLIVE values per study, keeping today's LUCIA values unchanged, with a test.

Split out of SW-589 so it does not block PR 5.
fields.summary: SW-589 follow-up: G17 - ReLIVE override values (DCU, period, tempr)

comments.body: <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Nguyen Ngoc Tram</custom> this is also completed in the db

<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Avichai Toubi</custom> 

1. Which table and column hold the ReLIVE DCU, period and temperature overrides, and what value is written? The pipeline recalculates aggregated_reason, and treats temper_reason as valid unless it starts with override.
2. The pipeline read a saved copy of the db, relive-clinical-2026-11-05-v2. Does thid copy include the db update? 
3. The code already has temperature limits (29–31) for the 7 ReLIVE PCBs. Should they be applied, or does the temper_reson from the db replace them when apply_overides ON?

content.text:
## Summary of today (2026-11-27)

- **PRs:** confirmed PR #52 merged, and you opened PRs 2–5. PR 3 is stacked on PR 2.
- **Branches:** split the report work out of PR 2's branch, rebased PR 3, and fixed PR 4's findings table and a commit attribution line.
- **PR 5:** changed estimation scoring as Avichai confirmed, then pushed it.
- **Records:** drafted the PR descriptions and updated the plan and handover.

## Email draft

```
Subject: Daily report 2026-11-27 - SW-589 (PR 38 review findings)

Hi all,

Done
- PR #52 (review triage and safe fixes) is merged.
- Opened four more PRs:
  - PR 2: preprocessing and feature selection
  - PR 3: splits, holdouts, training and default models (stacked on PR 2)
  - PR 4: report fixes and features-stage resume
  - PR 5: estimation stage and model cards
- PR 5 update, as agreed with Avichai: estimation now scores the training sensor type and breath by default, other breaths only when selected, and never other sensor types.
- Findings: 52 of 70 are resolved in the merged and open PRs (44 fixed, 7 won't fix, 1 covered by another item). G19 (database update) has since been completed by Tony.
- All SW-589 sub-tasks (SW-594 to SW-602) are Done.
- Trial merge of PRs 2-5: no code conflicts. Tests: 626 passed, 1 skipped, 6 expected failures, 1 known failure (SW-611), 1 known collection error (SW-610).

Blockers
- PRs 2-5 are waiting for review.
- Eran (8 items): Eran's preprocessing (SW-612), report methodology (SW-614 to SW-618) and GRID_CLEAN (SW-619, SW-620).
- Gilad and Avichai: default config values (SW-606) and the missing-value fill policy (SW-613).
- Tony, Lenny and Gilad: which model dashboard to integrate (SW-624).
- Avichai: my follow-up questions on the ReLIVE overrides (SW-622).
- Tony and Avichai: confirmation on the synthetic test dataset (SW-607).

Next steps
- Address review comments, then merge PR 2 first and point PR 3 to master.
- Resolve the findings file conflicts as the PRs merge.
- Add before/after metrics to the PRs.
- Update the findings file for G19, and for G17 once SW-622 is clarified.
- Fix SW-611.
- After PRs 2-4 merge: rebase PR 5 and write the user manual (SW-625).

SW-589 is due today. It stays In Progress until the PRs are reviewed and merged.

Best regards,
Tram
```

**Check before sending**
- **SW-622 and SW-623 are marked Done in Jira,** but the findings file on PR 5 still shows G17 and G19 as `WAITING`. Your three questions on SW-622 have no reply yet, so I listed it as a blocker.
- **Last paragraph:** keeping SW-589 In Progress is my assumption. Change it if you plan to close the ticket or ask for a new due date.
- **Test counts:** they're from the Windows trial merge; the latest PR 5 commits haven't been run on Linux.
- **Not in the email:** upgrade this machine's Git Credential Manager or switch to SSH before November 30.

I can also save this as `daily-reports/20261127.md` in your notes repo.
